proof_natural:
**Proposition.** For any category C, an object X ∈ Ob(C) is uniquely determined up to isomorphism by the functor Hom(-, X): C^op → Set, and for any number field K, its arithmetic properties are completely determined by the splitting behavior of primes encoded in the associated Galois representations.

**Proof.** We assume that C is a locally small category where Hom(A,B) is a set for all objects A,B, and that C has all necessary limits and colimits. For the number-theoretic portion, we work within ZFC set theory and assume the existence of absolute Galois groups with their profinite topology, the validity of the axiom of choice for constructing inverse limits, and the standard machinery of algebraic number theory including L-functions and their analytic continuation.

We begin with the categorical perspective. By the Yoneda Lemma, for any objects X,Y ∈ Ob(C), if there exists a natural isomorphism Hom(-,X) ≅ Hom(-,Y) between the contravariant hom-functors, then X ≅ Y. This fundamental result establishes that objects in a category are uniquely determined by the morphisms into them. The Yoneda embedding h: C → Fun(C^op, Set) defined by h(X) = Hom(-,X) is fully faithful, meaning that morphisms between objects correspond bijectively to natural transformations between their associated representable functors.

This principle of determination by relational structure extends to group theory through the Tannaka-Krein duality theorem. For a compact group G, the category Rep(G) of continuous finite-dimensional representations determines G up to isomorphism. The group can be reconstructed as the automorphisms of the forgetful functor from Rep(G) to vector spaces.

Turning to number fields, let K be a number field with absolute Galois group Gal(K̄/K). The category of Galois representations Rep(Gal(K̄/K)) encodes all arithmetic information about K, as the Galois group acts on all algebraic extensions and this action determines the splitting behavior of primes. 

For abelian extensions L/K, Class Field Theory provides an explicit description: the extension is completely determined by the kernel of the Artin reciprocity map CK → Gal(L/K), where CK denotes the idele class group. The splitting behavior of primes follows a precise pattern: a prime p splits completely in L/K if and only if its Frobenius element Frob_p lies in the kernel of this map.

For general Galois extensions L/K with Galois group G, the Chebotarev Density Theorem states that the proportion of primes whose Frobenius element lies in a given conjugacy class C equals |C|/|G|. This distribution of Frobenius elements among conjugacy classes determines the Galois group up to isomorphism. [Note: The claim that the multiset of conjugacy class sizes determines a finite group uniquely requires additional group-theoretic arguments not fully developed here.]

Thus we see a profound parallel: objects in categories are determined by morphisms into them (Yoneda), groups are determined by their representation categories (Tannaka-Krein), and number fields are determined by their Galois representations and the splitting behavior of primes (Class Field Theory and Chebotarev). In each case, the intrinsic structure is completely captured by relational or functorial data. This completes the proof. □
